reasons: r6 (rubric_r6) is unsatisfiable and self-contradictory: task.deliverables fixes a single 2D PNG at outputs/out1.png, and the instruction requires a 2D environment concept layout, yet rubric_r6 asks the worker to have committed to one branch '2D layout or 3D mock-up' and scores branch consistency. With a 2D-only deliverable mandated, the branch choice is pre-determined by the case author, not a worker professional judgment, so rubric_r6 cannot produce meaningful signal and contradicts r1's single-2D-artifact requirement. It cannot be traced to a distinct public task requirement beyond the original O*NET task's permissive '2D layouts or 3D mock-ups' phrasing, which the case itself already forecloses.

Requirement mapping is internally inconsistent. r1 maps to binding_i1 and binding_i2 only (both synthetic instructions), while r2-r6 map to binding_i1/i2/i3 including binding_i3. The artifact_d1 requirement maps all three. binding_i3 is listed with instruction:null and references[] empty, i.e. it supplies no actual requirement text; the rubric criteria (r2, r3, r4) nevertheless cite it as evidence. A required reference binding with no instruction and no bound content cannot substantiate the scored criteria attributed to it.

r4 asserts consistency with 'the proportions of the supplied character sheet' as a scored criterion, but the only character-sheet evidence is a model_observation_unverified segment description (seg_cf8a8048e5fc5133dfa8617b) plus a programmatic 1334x750 dimension record. No measured proportion relationships, no named rider, and no verified human-scale ratios are bound. The criterion asks the grader to validate proportion consistency against an unverified visual description, so the specified verification is not executable as written.

The case objective and r1 mandate 'approximately the references' aspect (about 1.78:1 = 1334x750)', but the referenced f_79d6f4de056ace187d8b1581 binding lists six panel segments at half-height crops (boxes with y-extent 0.5) plus a separate full-image dimension record. The 1334x750 figure is sourced only from programmatic extraction (source_located, not content-verified). Aspect is stated as both an authored preference (i2, synthetic_instruction) and as a property of 'the references'; the rubric presents 1.78:1 as a target grounded in reference geometry while the limitation text concedes no measured dimensions exist. That ambiguity makes the aspect tolerance in verification_spec undefined.

r2's conflict_policy and full_credit require that 'the reference panels are not reproduced or redistributed' and that the deliverable not 'imply affiliation'. This is a compliance/licence condition, not a visual outcome derivable from the assets (both files carry license_status unknown, redistribution_allowed false). It is scored under a semantic_guide on the delivered artwork, but a PNG cannot demonstrate non-affiliation or non-redistribution; there is no artifact-level observable that verifies this condition, so the criterion is unverifiable by the stated method.

r3 and r5 assert stylistic targets ('quiet, geometric, painterly-vector', 'strong horizontal layering', restrained palette). These trace to synthetic_instruction i1 and to unverified panel observations, not to any public task requirement. The underlying O*NET task ('Prepare two-dimensional concept layouts or three-dimensional mock-ups') contains no such style mandate. The audit must reject unsupported exact visual claims; here the entire style rubric rests on the model's own fallible descriptions of the reference sheet and on authored preferences.

No completed example solution or full source model is present in the graph, and neither reference is supplied as a finished answer, so no_answer_leakage passes. The procedural operations (i4-i7) trace forward to out1 and to r1-r5, and the artifact check (artifact_d1, file_exists on outputs/out1.png) is deterministic and correctly distinguished from the semantic criteria. However, verification_soundness fails: all five semantic rubric items are semantic_guide with no rendered-inspection verifier executed, the VLM segment descriptions are explicitly model_observation_unverified, and no modality necessity is established — i3's spatial hypothesis remains necessity_status 'hypothesis' with evidence_status 'unretrieved'.

Minimality is satisfied for a single-artifact case, but the rubric carries seven scored items for one image, of which r6 is non-actionable and r2 embeds a non-visual compliance condition; the set contains redundant/unsatisfiable criteria rather than the minimal criterion set needed for this task.
